evidence: Narrow confirmation of an acknowledged service-contract assumption, not a claim that either harness fails. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:248-258 require graph to reuse an existing summarizer occupant, post durable thread requests without waiting for prior summaries, have that occupant accept/dispatch/report them, and recover pending requests after occupant loss; they select no periodic model wake. Reproduction if an occupant's main turn ends after request A: graph sees it still present, so does not take the approved absent-occupant activation path; it posts request B, but the text specifies no bridge from a newly durable thread message to a fresh native turn or continuing receive loop. B remains pending with no dispatch/result, contrary to the approved ordinary summarizer's request-processing role (DESIGN-NOTES.md:247-258; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34). A request posted while a helper is active has the same unresolved receive boundary. Herdr does offer a possible external prompt surface: https://herdr.dev/docs/agent-automation/ says 'agent prompt submits text plus encoded Enter' and 'It can prompt an agent that is already working' (lines 132-138), but the design does not choose this or qualify a thread-driven equivalent. The cheapest closure is an end-to-end busy/idle/restart trace per intended harness, then specify a generic wake/resume path if needed. Durable pending storage prevents lost work; it does not itself make an existing idle occupant act.
